region.text: Transylvania and the Partium (the page names the Partium as 'the other major component' of the principality)

ledger.note: 1570: John II Sigismund Zapolya becomes prince of Transylvania under the Treaty of Speyer. 16 August 1570: he gave up his claim as King of Hungary; the treaty recognized the principality as belonging to the Hungarian kingdom under public law (infobox 'Established: Treaty of Speyer, 16 August 1570'); 'It existed as an Ottoman vassal state for the majority of the 16th and 17th centuries'. The page names Transylvania and the Partium, not a boundary; the drawn core is Cliopatria's Eastern Hungarian Kingdom shape of 1564-1571.

region.text: Transylvania, where Michael entered the capital Gyulafehervar after Andrew Bathory was killed on 3 November

ledger.note: October 1599: Michael the Brave of Wallachia takes Transylvania as imperial governor. 'On 18 October 1599 Michael won a decisive victory' at Selimbar over Cardinal Andrew Bathory's army; he became 'the imperial governor (i.e. de facto ruler) of Transylvania, under Habsburg suzerainty' (infobox October 1599-September 1600). Owner's record: the counterpart is the occupier, matching the Wallachia dossier's own occupation_start.

September 1600: Michael is driven out of Transylvania. Hungarian nobles backed by Basta and the Austrian forces defeated him at Miraslau, 'forcing the prince to leave Transylvania'; the body gives no date for the battle, the infobox ends his Transylvanian rule in September 1600.

region.text: Transylvania, governed by General Giorgio Basta for the Habsburgs

ledger.note: 1600: the Habsburgs rule through General Basta. 'General Giorgio Basta's governance of Transylvania faced significant opposition from the Hungarian nobility.' The month follows Michael's expulsion (page gives no date for Basta's start); Michael was killed on 9 August 1601 on Basta's order.

21 February 1605: Stephen Bocskai is elected Prince of Transylvania at Nyárádszereda, ending Habsburg rule. The Bocskai page: the delegates 'elected him prince in Nyárádszereda' on 21 February 1605 (and acclaimed him prince of Hungary at Szerencs on 20 April 1605). The Transylvania page has 'After 1601 the principality was for a short time under the rule of Rudolf II' and Bocskay's 'successful rebellion against Austrian rule' from 1604 to 1606; its sentence 'Bocskay was elected Prince of Transylvania on 5 April 1603' contradicts both its own 1604-1606 dates and the Bocskai page. Reviewer fix 2026-10-31 (was 1603-04).

region.text: Habsburg-controlled Royal Hungary, whose north Bethlen 'fully conquered' (the land Cliopatria drops from the Habsburg Monarchy in 1622)

ledger.note: August 1619: Gabriel Bethlen invades Habsburg Royal Hungary. The Bethlen page: 'In August 1619, Bethlen invaded Royal Hungary'; 'In September, he took Kassa'; 'In October 1619, Bethlen took Pressburg'. The Nikolsburg page's 'invaded Habsburg-controlled Royal Hungary in 1618 and fully conquered its north until 1620' is a year early; it also has a peace of January 1620 giving Bethlen '13 counties in eastern Royal Hungary' and the emperor reconquering 'most of Royal Hungary by 1621'. Reviewer fix 2026-10-31 (was 1618).
31 December 1621: the Peace of Nikolsburg ends the war between Bethlen and Ferdinand II ('signed on 31 December 1621 in Nikolsburg').

region.text: 'seven counties around the Upper Tisza River (in present-day Slovakia, Ukraine, Hungary, and Romania)' and 'the fortresses of Tokaj, Munkács, and Ecsed'

ledger.note: 31 December 1621: Bethlen receives seven counties in northern Hungary at Nikolsburg. The Transylvania page: 'seven additional counties in northern Hungary'. The page does not list the counties; the drawn region is the land Cliopatria drops from the Habsburg Monarchy in 1622 (the same region as that dossier's loss event), which is also the 10,369 km2 Cliopatria adds to Transylvania in 1622. He also received 'a duchy in Silesia' (not drawn).

27 August 1660: Nagyvárad falls to the Ottomans and becomes the seat of a pasha. 'The fall of Nagyvárad to the expansionist Ottomans on 27 August 1660 marked the decline of the Principality.' Second page: the Varat Eyalet article says the eyalet was 'formed in 1660' with Varat 'the seat of an Ottoman governor (Beylerbey) in 1660'. The page names the city; the district is Cliopatria's 10 cells around Oradea.

1692: the capital moves from Gyulafehervar (Alba Iulia) to Cibinium (Sibiu). Infobox: 'Gyulafehérvár (Alba Iulia), 1570–1692; Cibinium (Nagyszeben/Hermannstadt/Sibiu), 1692–1711'. region.text: Transylvania, 'formally attached to Habsburg-controlled Hungary, and subjected to the direct rule of the emperor's governors'

ledger.note: 26 January 1699: the Treaty of Karlowitz passes Transylvania to the Habsburgs. 'Following the 1699 Treaty of Karlowitz, Transylvania was formally attached to Habsburg-controlled Hungary, and subjected to the direct rule of the emperor's governors.' Great Turkish War page: Karlowitz 'secured territories, the rest of Hungary and overlordship of Transylvania for the Austrians'. The infobox keeps the principality to 29 April 1711 (Peace of Szatmar); that later span is Habsburg-governed and is not drawn as a separate state.

wars.name: Gabriel Bethlen's war in Royal Hungary
wars.outcome: Bethlen won seven counties around the Upper Tisza, the fortresses of Tokaj, Munkács and Ecsed, a Silesian duchy and the title of imperial prince at the Peace of Nikolsburg, 31 December 1621; the emperor 'reconquer[ed] most of Royal Hungary by 1621'.
wars.note: The page's 1618 start is its own wording ('invaded ... in 1618 and fully conquered its north until 1620'); a peace of January 1620 gave Bethlen 13 counties and he 'resumed the war in September'. Not a Wikipedia article title.

wars.name: Michael the Brave's conquest of Transylvania (Battle of Șelimbăr)
wars.outcome: Michael beat Cardinal Andrew Bathory at Selimbar on 18 October 1599 and ruled as imperial governor to September 1600, when Hungarian nobles and Basta beat him at Miraslau; he was killed on 9 August 1601.
wars.note: Not a Wikipedia article title; the Michael the Brave page carries the account.

wars.name: Bocskai uprising
wars.outcome: Bocskai's successful rebellion (28 September 1604-23 June 1606) ended with the Treaty of Vienna, recognizing him as sovereign prince of an 'enlarged Principality of Transylvania' with religious liberty and the right to elect princes.
wars.note: No territorial gain is named on the page, so no zone is given; unresolved, see notes.

wars.name: Ottoman and Tatar wars on Transylvania (George II Rakoczi's Polish campaign and its aftermath)
wars.outcome: 'In 1657, George II Rákóczi invaded the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth'; wars then ravaged the principality from 1657 to 1661 ('the Partium and the counties of Belső-Szolnok, Doboka, Kolozs, Közép-Szolnok, and Kraszna were laid waste'); Nagyvárad fell to the Ottomans on 27 August 1660.
wars.note: Not a Wikipedia article title. The diet under Prince Kemény declared Transylvania's secession from the Ottomans in April 1661 and appealed to Vienna.

wars.name: Great Turkish War

zones.text: 'Turkish resistance collapsed throughout the region as far away as Transylvania and Serbia' (Buda fell 2 September 1686)

wars.outcome: The Habsburgs won; the Treaty of Karlowitz (26 January 1699) 'secured territories, the rest of Hungary and overlordship of Transylvania for the Austrians'.
wars.note: The page's infobox dates Karlowitz 26 January 1699 and its body 22 January 1699. It says nothing on Transylvania between 1683 and 1699 beyond the sentences quoted.

The Ottoman Varat Eyalet and Habsburg fronts move with the Great Turkish War; Karlowitz (1699) is a treaty but the page names no boundary.

notes: Written by eu-15-k on 2026-10-25 from six pages (page budget 5 plus the Upper Hungary page that belongs to the next dossier's budget). (1) END DATE: Cliopatria ends the row in 1695 and its Habsburg Monarchy shape holds Transylvania from 1696; the Transylvania infobox ends the principality at the Peace of Szatmar, 29 April 1711. This dossier ends it at the Treaty of Karlowitz, 26 January 1699, where the page puts Transylvania under the emperor's governors and the Habsburg dossier dates its gain of Transylvania; a gap-filler may prefer 1711, in which case 1699-1711 needs a keyframe and the Habsburg shape must leave Transylvania out. (2) OTTOMAN SUZERAINTY is not an event type for the vassal. The ottoman-empire dossier holds vassal_start 1526 and vassal_end 1699 for principality-of-transylvania; the Transylvania page says it was an Ottoman vassal state 'for the majority of the 16th and 17th centuries' and that the diet declared secession in April 1661. The Ottoman dossier has no Nagyvarad/Varat event for 1660 (loss recorded here against ottoman-empire), and no Habsburg protectorate over Transylvania 1687-1699 appears on any page opened (Treaty of Blaj, 1687, is not on the Transylvania or Great Turkish War pages): unverified. (3) TREATY OF VIENNA 1606: the page says Bocskai was recognized as prince of an 'enlarged' principality but names no land besides the Partium, and Cliopatria's shape does not change in 1606 (101,150 km2 from 1595 to 1621). A gap-filler should open 'Peace of Vienna (1606)' to find what was added. (4) NIKOLSBURG COUNTIES: the pages do not list the seven counties or say how long Transylvania held them (only that the Peace of Linz 1645 confirmed the Vienna articles); Cliopatria draws them to 1682. (5) UPPER HUNGARY: the 1682-1685 transfer of 23,014 km2 between Transylvania and the Principality of Upper Hungary rests on Cliopatria's shapes only (confidence 1); the Upper Hungary page says Transylvania supported the rising. The Habsburg dossier's 1685 gain of Upper Hungary covers only Slovakia and Borsod-Abauj-Zemplen, so who held the rest in 1686 is open. (6) NOISE: Cliopatria's cells are about 253 km2; changes of two cells or fewer in 1595, 1670 and 1673 are not given events. (7) PARTIAL PAGES: WebFetch summarises pages, so quotations above are the fetched answers to targeted questions; 'Eyalet of Varat' and 'Oradea Eyalet' returned not found. (8) RULERS: the Transylvania page lists only the first (John II Sigismund Zapolya, 1570-1571) and last (Francis II Rakoczi, 1704-1711) prince in its infobox, so no ruler strip is given. (9) GAZETTEER: no unknown names; Tokaj and Munkacs are not in places.jsonl and are cited in text only.
